newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson disappointed by Great Western.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson disappointed by Great Western.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co, which raised its offer for Great Western Financial Corp, said it was disappointed Great Western urged its stockholders not to sign a consent solicitation sent by Ahmanson.
"Great Western stockholders have absolutely nothing to lose by voting in favor of our consent proposals," said Ahmanson.

Meanwhile, a source near the Washington Mutual/Great Western transaction said Ahmanson's projections were overly-aggressive and that Ahmanson's proposed merger might face problems at the Office of Thrift Supervision.
"The combined company's (Ahmanson/Great Western) tangible equity to assets ratio would be 3.85 at closing, which the Office of Thrift Supervision may find a problem," said the source.
An Ahmanson spokesman had no immediate comment. Washington Mutual is meeting with investors this week do discuss its bid, which it still believes is superior.
Ahmanson said that any suggestions that it would face regulatory difficulties in a merger with Great Western were outrageous.
"Ahmanson is well-capitalized by every recognized regulatory standard and combined with Great Western, we will remain well-capitalized," a spokesman said.
